headline: Rwanda plans a 6km circuit with 197 metres of elevation change
body: Rwanda's proposed African Grand Prix circuit will run anti-clockwise over 6km, with 17 corners and 197 metres of elevation change across a lap. Alex Wurz and Carsten Tilke are designing the Bugesera venue around two hills and a lake, with cambered corners and banking. The full layout and inaugural race date have yet to be announced.

headline: FIA tightens floor-support geometry for 2027
body: The published 2027 technical rules limit the rounded junction between a floor support and other bodywork to a 5mm radius. They also restrict where those supports can meet bodywork, narrowing the freedom to use them to shape airflow around the car. The changes apply next season.

headline: Waché sees more potential in Red Bull's engine programme
body: Pierre Waché rates Red Bull's first in-house power-unit project at four or five out of ten and says there is considerable scope to improve. He says integrating the chassis and engine departments remains a learning process because they work differently and engine development takes longer.
